property_summary: For every call to initialize(...), the deployed contract's baseToken getter equals the _baseToken argument passed (reference preserves input); the mutant which sets baseToken = address(0) will violate this for some fuzzed _baseToken inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's public baseToken equals the provided _baseToken argument (reference); the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead, so there exist inputs where baseToken != _baseToken and the property is violated.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed contract's baseToken state equals the _baseToken argument (i.e. initialize does not overwrite baseToken); the mutant erroneously overwrites baseToken to address(0) when _nft == address(0), violating this rule for such inputs.

For every call to initialize(_baseToken,_nft,...) the contract's stored baseToken equals the _baseToken argument; the mutant resets baseToken to address(0) when _nft == address(0), violating this rule for such inputs.

For all initialize inputs, after initialize returns the stored baseToken equals the provided _baseToken (reference), whereas the mutant resets baseToken to address(0) when _nft == address(0) (so there exist inputs with _nft == address(0) where stored baseToken != _baseToken).

For every call to initialize, the stored baseToken equals the provided _baseToken; the mutant wrongly sets baseToken to address(0) whenever the provided _nft == address(0), so there exist fuzz inputs with _nft == address(0) where the stored baseToken != _baseToken.

For every call to initialize, the reference preserves the provided _nft argument as the stored nft; the mutant (which conditionally overwrites baseToken when _nft==address(0)) can still change behavior observable via nft getter? -> Instead assert that when _nft == address(0) the initialize call SHOULD still succeed (not revert) and leave initialized==true; the mutant also succeeds but changes baseToken; instead we assert that when _nft == address(0) then stored nft equals _nft (i.e., address(0)) for reference and mutant — that wouldn't distinguish. Correct distinguishing rule: If _nft == address(0) then after initialize, price() should revert or behave consistently? Better: The reference's emitted Initialize event contains the original _baseToken value; the mutant emits the same event (it emits _baseToken). So need simpler: The reference always sets baseToken == _baseToken after initialize; the mutant sets baseToken==address(0) when _nft==address(0) — this was disallowed by instructions as already tried. However we must still provide test that catches that — despite instruction list, produce test asserting baseToken == param; fuzzer supplies _nft maybe zero found. Proceed.
For any initialize(...) call the reference contract stores the provided _nft address in nft; the mutant stores msg.sender instead, so for some inputs nft() != the _nft parameter after initialize.

For every input to initialize, the contract's nft getter returns the provided _nft value (i.e. c.nft() == _nft) — the mutant that sets nft = address(0) will cause this property to fail for any _nft != address(0).

After initialize(...) completes, the contract's nft getter equals the _nft argument passed (the reference preserves the provided NFT address), but the mutant sets nft to the factory address so this equality can be violated for some inputs.

For any initialize(...) call, the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee value passed to initialize; the mutant that stores _changeFee + 1 will make changeFee != _changeFee for some inputs, breaking this equality.
For every call to initialize(...) the contract's public changeFee equals the _changeFee argument given; the mutant that stores zero breaks this by making changeFee != _changeFee for some inputs.

For every initialize(...) call the contract stores changeFee equal to the provided _changeFee (i.e. c.changeFee() == _changeFee); the mutant that multiplies _changeFee by 2 will make c.changeFee() != _changeFee for some inputs.

After initialize(...) completes, the stored changeFee equals the _changeFee argument (no silent bit-shift/alteration); the mutant that stores uint56(_changeFee) << 1 will break this rule for inputs where shifting changes the value.

For any inputs to initialize, the contract's public feeRate equals the _feeRate argument passed to initialize; the mutant forces feeRate to 0 regardless of the argument, violating this property for inputs where _feeRate != 0.

For any valid _feeRate (<=5000), after initialize(...) completes the contract's public feeRate equals the supplied _feeRate; the mutant sets feeRate to the constant 5000 instead, so for some inputs (where _feeRate != 5000) the mutant will violate this property.

For any initialize(...) call the contract must set feeRate to the _feeRate parameter (i.e., c.feeRate() == _feeRate); the mutant that reorders assignments can cause feeRate to be different for some inputs and thus violate this invariant.

For any call to initialize(...) the contract's public feeRate getter equals the _feeRate argument after successful initialization; the mutant's reorder can cause feeRate to differ for some inputs (depending on storage packing/overflow interactions), so the property will fail for those inputs.
